newsitem.title: USA: Hansol Telecom plans transpacific cable.
newsitem.headline: Hansol Telecom plans transpacific cable.

text.p: Hansol Telecom said Wednesday it plans to form a multinational consortium to build and operate a high-capacity fiber optic cable across the Pacific Ocean.
Hansol said it expects construction of the cable, which would connect Korea and Japan directly with North America, to cost between $750 million and $850 million.
A division of Korea's Hansol Group, Hansol Telecom said it is in active discussions with multiple international and U.S. carriers and expects to form a consortium within the next two months.
Hansol Telecom's chief executive, Jin Soh, said he expects the proposed APII cable project to challenge the dominant players, AT&T Corp and Japan's Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD).

"The APII will break the dominance of AT&T and KDD over transpacific cable traffic and will offer a cost-efective alternative to international carriers in Asian counties beginning in 1999," Soh said in a company statement.
